      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story</link>
      <description><p>After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’</p><p>The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.</p><p>Kundizeza’s story <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a4f3fb6a6178e0225b39a4c/t/6a95fffc36f1fc568e02f7fe/1788215293124/3.The+Blue+Fighter.pdf">The Blue Fighter</a>, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/6487803463c6c4e3138642f657eeb1cd90cd5acc/0_111_1078_862/master/1078.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=e825c93b0c4e49e69e380953e02995c6">

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Fri, 13 Nov 2026 19:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight ]]> Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand.

I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again.

This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky.

The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars. In fact, you're likely to catch their collective brightness in your peripheral vision every time you go outside and look up.

But every November the Pleiades remind me that naked-eye observing isn't as simple as opening the back door and looking up. How many Pleiades I can see can change depending on what I do during the next 10 minutes.

What's happening and when to look

The Pleiades, also known as Messier 45 (M45) or the "Seven Sisters," are an open star cluster in Taurus. They're one of the closest clusters to the solar system and some of the youngest stars you can see with the naked eye — just 100 million years old. They're basically newborns.

In mid-November, they rise in the east in the early evening and climb higher as the night progresses, making this an excellent time to get acquainted with them. Look east after dark for a tiny, compact group of stars. If you know Orion, which rises later, the Pleiades are above and to the right of it from mid-northern latitudes. Nearby you'll also find orange Aldebaran and the much broader V-shaped Hyades cluster. The Hyades are closer to the sun, but their stars are about 625 million years old.

The name "Seven Sisters" creates an immediate observational trap: people assume they're supposed to see seven stars. That's not necessarily true. In fact, six is a common naked-eye result under decently dark conditions (note that the shape of the six brightest is like a mini Big Dipper/Plough), while people with sharp eyesight under darker skies may see more. The cluster itself contains about 1,000 stars. The number you personally distinguish depends on eyesight, sky brightness, atmospheric conditions and how well your eyes have adapted to darkness.

That makes M45 much more interesting to me than a simple tick-box target. So tonight, don't just find the Pleiades — count them.

How and when I'm watching it

I'm going to run my Pleiades eye test in stages. First, I'll step outside and look almost immediately. I'll count the individual stars I can distinguish without spending ages convincing myself about marginal ones. Then I'll wait. After about 10 minutes (without looking at my phone or bright outdoor lights, of course), I'll count again. Full dark adaptation takes considerably longer, but even 10 minutes can make an obvious difference when you've just come from a brightly lit house.

I'll then try my trusty 10x50 binoculars. This is where the experiment stops being subtle. The little naked-eye knot of brightness suddenly becomes a field filled with stars. The Pleiades don't just become brighter through binoculars. Their whole character changes because stars that were below my naked-eye threshold appear. I'll also use the averted vision technique, looking slightly to one side rather than directly at M45. It's one of the best demonstrations of the technique, with its fainter stars seemingly popping into view as your more light-sensitive peripheral vision takes over.

Stargazer's corner: November 13-19, 2026

The moon is returning to the evening sky this week, waxing from a thin crescent toward first quarter. It reaches first quarter around Nov. 17, so moonlight becomes progressively more noticeable during the first half of the night. Look southwest during twilight, and you'll see the beautiful sight of a crescent moon sporting Earthshine, sunlight reflected from Earth onto the moon's night side.

Overnight, Nov. 15-16, don't miss Mars and Jupiter in conjunction. The two planets will appear just over a degree apart, rising in the east during the evening before climbing high into the southern sky in the hours before sunrise.

The following night, Nov. 17-18, the Leonid meteor shower peaks. This is one shower where staying up later actually matters. Leo, the constellation containing the shower's radiant, doesn't rise until late, so the better opportunity comes after midnight and toward the predawn hours.

Asterism of the week: The Kids

Auriga, "the Charioteer," is easy to see in the northeastern and eastern sky during November evenings, but have you spied the asterism close to its brightest star, Capella? It's known as the "Goat Star," though its Latin name is the diminutive of capra, meaning "little she-goat." The reason is esoteric — Capella represents Amalthea, the mythological goat that suckled the infant Zeus — but there is a neat asterism (shape of stars) nearby that suddenly makes sense. Close to Capella is a triangle of faint stars that are known as The Kids — Epsilon, Zeta and Eta Aurigae — traditionally imagined as the offspring of Capella. It's one of those little patterns that makes a constellation much easier to recognize.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Martian Isolation' is an upcoming sci-fi survival horror game that looks like 'The Martian' and 'Event Horizon' had a horrific child ]]>

"Martian Isolation" is an upcoming single-player, first-person survival horror game that's just been revealed with a suitably creepy launch trailer. And yes, it does look an awful lot like "The Martian," doesn't it?

There's a lot of survival gameplay on display here that mirrors Mark Watney's tale of survival on the Red Planet, as your stranded protagonist is forced to explore the Martian surface to acquire resources, grow plants, and repair their base.

That comparison to Andy Weir's sci-fi masterpiece does fall away as you get further into the trailer, though, when the horror part of the game's description comes into play: Flickering lights, creepy figures stalking the halls of your Martian habitat, and blood dripping from the walls.

Oh yeah, that's some good creepy sci-fi horror right there. It's giving "Event Horizon", and that's always getting a thumbs-up from me.

There's no release date scheduled at this time, with the 'Martian Isolation' Steam page simply listing it as "coming soon," though the YouTube trailer description does say it "will be available on Steam in 2027".

You can't pre-order yet, but if this looks like your jam, you can add it to your wishlist.

Beyond that, we know shockingly little about this title. It's the debut game from Golden Milestone Studio, but there's very little information out there beyond a name. The latest blog post on the game's Steam page says that they're a "small team," but what we've seen so far is encouraging.

There seems to be a pronounced split between the survival and horror elements of the game along the day/night cycle. Daytime sees you exploring the Martian surface, smashing rocks, cleaning solar panels, and doing sick jumps on a quad bike.

The psychological torment only begins once the sun goes down (they mostly come out at night … mostly), as your character starts encountering cosmic horrors and weird naked zombie men.

Are they hallucinations, or is there some malevolent presence hiding in the blood-red sands of Mars?

I'm always looking for new ways to shatter my psyche and possibly soil my pants, so I'll be keeping a close eye on this one. In the meantime, I do need to get back and finish "Routine." I left my character hiding under a desk months ago, and I haven't been brave enough to go back. As Mama always said, you can't have any Martian horror until you finish your lunar horror first.

]]> <![CDATA[ Astronomers trace mystery radio signals back to cosmic odd couple of white dwarf and sun-like star ]]>

Astronomers have traced a mysterious radio signal back to a cosmic odd couple comprised of a dead star, a white dwarf, and its stellar companion, a sun-like star.

The white dwarf in the newly discovered system, designated GPM J071507−114153 and located around 5,000 light-years away, spins once every eight minutes, sending out radio pulses. These radio pulses have been seen from binary systems with smaller and cooler red dwarf stars before, but rarely from a system like GPM J071507−114153.

GPM J071507−114153 belongs to a class of celestial objects called long-period transients (LPTs) known to produce radio signals that switch on and off over intervals of minutes or hours. Around a dozen LPTs have been detected since the team behind this research found the first in 2021. Several previously discovered LPT systems contain a white dwarf and a companion star, but it has been unclear which of the two stars was generating the radio pulses. That means the discovery of GPM J071507−114153 and finding that the pulses come from close to the white dwarf could be a significant step toward understanding the nature of LPTs.

"This is the first time the pulses are clear enough to see the white dwarf moving in its orbit around its companion," team leader and commissioning scientist with the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKA), Sam McSweeney, said in a statement. "So we know that the pulsations are coming from a region close to the white dwarf, or possibly even from the white dwarf itself."

The pulses seen by the team also allowed them to detect stellar flares erupting on the sun-like star.

"As a bonus, we also saw the white dwarf moving behind a region with a strong magnetic field, most likely a 'stellar prominence,' which is a large loop of plasma erupting from a star's surface," team member Natasha Hurley-Walker of the International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research (ICRAR), Curtin University, Australia, said. "It's amazing that by using radio wavelengths we can detect the storms on a star over 5,000 light-years away."

Hurley-Walker and the team at ICRAR have been at the cutting edge of rare star systems like this.

"We detected this system in a large survey using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) to scan the entire Milky Way visible from Australia," Hurley-Walker said. "We then used the MeerKAT radio telescope in South Africa to determine its precise position."

After the radio telescopes detected this LPT, it was confirmed using the W.M. Keck Observatory on Maunakea in Hawaii. The visible light follow-up of Keck also confirmed that the star in GPM J071507−114153 was a G-type star, just like the sun.

MeerKAT and the MWA are both precursors for the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), the world’s largest and most sensitive radio telescope project. That means the future is bright for LPTs.

"If we are already making such discoveries with precursor telescopes, just imagine how many more star systems we will be able to find, and what a beautifully detailed view of their signals we will have, once the SKA telescopes are completely built," McSweeney said.

The team's research was published on Thursday (Nov. 12) in the journal Nature Astronomy.

]]> <![CDATA[ Netflix’s ‘Ray Gunn’ gets 2nd trailer, and we're hyped for this animated sci-fi noir from ‘Incredibles’ director Brad Bird ]]>

Dreaming of a bright and shiny future filled with personal jet packs, levitating autos, and automated gadgets straight out of "The Jetsons?" Add in a gritty mystery, a notorious private eye, double-crossing aliens, and a bombshell diva framed for a killing, and you’ve got the perfect recipe for "Ray Gunn."

Oscar-winning director Brad Bird ("The Incredibles," "Ratatouille") returns to our screens with his new big-budget animated sci-fi project, "Ray Gunn," and this latest trailer has us primed.

"In Metropia, a gigantic city in an alternate future as seen from 1939, private eye Raymond Gunn (Sam Rockwell) is drawn into a case involving aliens, murder, and a multimedia starlet named Venus Nova (Scarlett Johansson)," states the official synopsis.

Netflix Films and Skydance Animation's "Ray Gunn" is a stylistic pastiche of classic film noir tropes populated by down-and-out detectives and femme fatales living in the inspiring air of technological optimism viewed through a pre-war America lens.

Think "The Fifth Element" meets "Who Framed Roger Rabbit?" and "The Maltese Falcon," and you’re going to be close to this sci-fi whodunnit's vibe, which is intended for more mature audiences and rated PG.

This energetic new preview is locked and loaded with dazzling visuals by Cinesite, freaky creatures, streamlined flying cars, and a blistering pace. And if you listen very closely, The B-52s' "Planet Claire" can be heard playing in the background, which is one of the touchstones that inspired Bird to begin his 36-year journey to bring "Ray Gunn" to life. Was it worth the wait? We'll have to find out.

Also starring the vocal talents of Tom Waits, Bobby Cannavale, Alan Tudyk, Matt Berry, and Michelle Rodriguez, "Ray Gunn" opens in select theaters and 70mm screenings Dec. 4. After that, it lands on Netflix on Dec. 18... a date you might want to circle on your calendar, as that’s also the release slot for "Avengers: Doomsday" and "Dune: Part 3."

It's going to be a busy day for sci-fi fans. "Strap in, buster!"

New Yorkers got a space-y surprise on Wednesday (Nov. 11): Retired NASA astronaut and U.S. Navy Captain Sunita "Suni" Williams rolled down 5th Avenue in the back of a classic convertible wrapped in patriotic decals as Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade.

What is it?

On Wednesday, New York City's 107th annual Veterans Day Parade made its way through Manhattan to the cheers and respectful nods of thousands of onlookers.

The parade is an annual tradition on the holiday, which honors veterans of the U.S. armed forces. As part of the parade, veterans, active-duty soldiers, firefighters, marching bands, youth cadets and more march through the city and honor those who have served and sacrificed in the U.S. military.

This year, the parade featured Suni Williams as its grand marshal. "I’m proud to join New Yorkers and Americans from around the country in honoring the service, sacrifice, and commitment of veterans from every generation," she said during the event.

Why is it incredible?

Williams was selected for NASA's astronaut program in 1998 and retired from it in December 2025. She spent 608 days in space during her astronaut career, the second-most by an American astronaut behind Peggy Whitson, who racked up 695.

Williams also had an extensive career in the U.S. Navy. She began as an ensign in 1987 before serving in a number of different roles. For example, she was a diving officer and a naval aviator and also provided helicopter combat support during Operation Desert Shield and Operation Provide Comfort. She further served as a squadron safety officer and finally as a captain, a rank she achieved in 2017.

During this time, Williams supported relief efforts following Hurricane Andrew, trained within the U.S. Naval Test Pilot School and gained a wealth of further experience flying as a military pilot.

Williams is part of a longstanding tradition of astronauts serving in the U.S. military. From test pilots to naval officers and more, there's a strong link between the U.S. armed forces and NASA's astronaut program.

If all goes well, the mission — which you can watch here at Space.com — will end on Saturday (Nov. 14) with the first attempt at what SpaceX itself calls the "Holy Grail of rocketry": Catching both Starship's Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage chopstick-style back at the launch pad.

"If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," SpaceX wrote in its Flight 15 mission description.

The 75-minute Flight 15 launch window opens today at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT), and a number of Starship firsts are planned for early in the flight. For example, while SpaceX has caught three Super Heavy boosters and reused two of them to date, the first attempt to catch a next-gen Super Heavy "V3" vehicle will come today, around 6.5 minutes after liftoff.

If the Ship upper stage gets the go-ahead for orbital insertion, it will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites — designed especially for use on Starship — into low Earth orbit (LEO), starting about 35 minutes after launch. Then, 21 hours later, if "internally developed, and FAA-approved, conditions" for a return to Starbase and catch are met — including on-orbit assessment of Ship's heat shield by three of the V3 satellites — SpaceX will attempt to recover the orbital upper stage.

This landmark try will follow the first-ever Ship reentry over inhabited areas, as the vehicle will maneuver its way over sparsely populated regions of northern Mexico and southern Texas. (On previous missions, Ship has splashed down in the open ocean.) It will head back to Starbase and make a bellyflop maneuver as it descends to the site's Pad 2 before flipping itself vertical, ready for embrace of the launch tower's waiting mechanical arms.

"SpaceX will attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and Starship on the upcoming flight. If both are successful, it will mark the first time that all parts of an orbital rocket return to Earth intact," Elon Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Nov. 6. "This is the critical breakthrough needed to make life multiplanetary."

The catch

Half of the system is already proven. With catching and reflying boosters largely established, the next and unprecedented step is catching Ship. This is no easy task. The vehicle, returning from orbital speeds, must survive the heat of reentry, make its way precisely back to the pad put itself in position to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. The full recovery of an orbital launch system would, in the words of SpaceX, be a "breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket" and would open the "door to airplane-like cadence."

A successful catch would allow SpaceX to then work on refurbishing Ship for reflight, the next challenge of full reusability. Musk said in August in a SpaceX earnings call that the company will aim to refly the Super Heavy and Ship early next year.

SpaceX has a lot of experience with rocket reuse, as its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket pioneered the practice. But the company is eyeing another level of reflight with Starship: It's targeting roughly 10,000 launches of the megarocket per year by 2030, which works out to more than one launch per hour.

"We're aiming to reach 30+ Starship launches/day in 2030, which is ~10k annualized," Musk posted on X in August.

Why so many launches?

The company has repeated that figure to regulators. In comments filed with the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration in late October, it said that "SpaceX anticipates conducting 10,000 launches per year itself." Meanwhile, the recently signed National Space Transportation Policy aims to boost the U.S.'s capabilities to support more than 1,000 rocket launches per year by 2030.

Musk added that SpaceX's planned Starbase Louisiana site alone could support that many Starship launches. For context: SpaceX launched 165 Falcon 9 missions in 2025, and that was about half of the global total for orbital flights.

Why is SpaceX targeting this incredible increase in launch cadence? It wants to build satellite megaconstellations that dwarf anything the world has ever seen.

The company's V3 Starlink satellites are too large to fly efficiently on the Falcon 9. Each one of the next-gen spacecraft adds 1 terabit of capacity to SpaceX's broadband network, and the 26 flying on Flight 15 are equivalent to around 10 Falcon 9 launches packed with Starlink V2 Mini satellites, according to SpaceX. And the company wants to put a staggering 100,000 V3 Starlink satellites into orbit. (There are currently about 11,000 current-gen Starlink satellites in orbit, and that's by far the largest satellite network assembled to date.)

The gap between SpaceX's vision and the situation today is vast. Starship flew four times in 2024 and five times in 2025, and Flight 15 would be its fourth launch of 2026. Starbase in Texas is currently authorized for 25 launches per year, and the Louisiana site is not expected to host a launch before 2029.

Even a perfect outing for Flight 15 and two clean catches will leave lots of work to do. SpaceX will then need to demonstrate reflight with Ship, after assessing the impact on its heat shield system. Then comes orbital refueling, which is a necessary step for any Starship trip beyond LEO and a requirement for SpaceX's commitment to NASA's Artemis program of moon exploration. It's unclear how many tanker flights and refuelings will be needed to make a lunar mission possible, but, whatever the number, Starship will probably need to be rapidly reusable. SpaceX has tested life support hardware on the ground in a crew cabin for the moon lander version of Starship that it is building for NASA, but no Starship has flown with such a system.

There are no guarantees for Flight 15. Ship will only be cleared for a return to Starbase and a catch attempt if it meets safety checks after reaching orbit, which itself is an achievement not to be taken for granted. Flight controllers may end up needing to bring Ship down in the Pacific Ocean or divert its reentry into the Gulf late into flight.

 <description>Od pátečního poledne je v provozu nový úsek silnice I/9 z Českolipska směrem do Šluknovského výběžku. <description>Univerzita Karlova ře&#353;í v posledních dnech kybernetický incident. &#352;kola uvedla, že se útočníkům podařilo proniknout přes napadenou webovou aplikaci do centrálního Studijního informačního systému (SIS). &#8222;Dosavadní technické &#353;etření potvrdilo, že útočník neoprávněně získal a stáhl část údajů evidovaných v SIS, včetně osobních údajů. <description>Česká technologická společnost AŽD roz&#353;ířila testování svého experimentálního autonomního vozidla EDITA o satelitní připojení Starlink. <description>Evropská unie dál zpřísňuje pravidla pro čínská online trži&#353;tě. Od července 2028 budou platformy ze zemí mimo EU, včetně Temu, Shein nebo AliExpress, odpovídat za výběr a odvod DPH ze v&#353;ech prodávaných zásilek bez ohledu na jejich hodnotu.  <description>Krakovská prokuratura obdržela oznámení na jednoho z policistů, který v sobotu zasáhl proti střelci v centru města. Útočník zastřelil nejprve tři členy své rodiny a následně šest náhodných kolemjdoucích na krakovském náměstí a patnáct dalších lidí zranil. Po přestřelce s policií pachatel v nemocnici zemřel.  <description>Nejméně jeden člověk přišel o život a 50 dalších, včetně osmi dětí, utrpělo zranění při opakovaných ruských útocích na Záporoží na jihovýchodě Ukrajiny. Při rozebírání trosek poškozené budovy zahynul další člověk, záchranář, na něhož spadl betonový panel, oznámil v pátek šéf regionální vojenské správy Mychajlo Semikin, který dříve informoval o stoupajícím počtu raněných. Rusové zasáhli blíže neurčený průmyslový objekt a pětipodlažní obytný dům.</description>

Ve čtvrtek to podle webu Politico řekl v rozhovoru s konzervativním rozhlasovým moderátorem Hughem Hewittem.  <description>Lídři evropských zemí se v pátek dopoledne sejdou v Dublinu na neformálním summitu Evropské unie. Chtějí probírat hlavně umělou inteligenci, například její dopady na společnost, bezpečnost a důvěru. Řešit chtějí rovněž potenciál AI k posílení evropské konkurenceschopnosti. „Ameriku nedoženeme dalšími pravidly, ale investicemi a rychlostí,“ řekl pro ranní vysílání Radiožurnálu vládní zmocněnec pro umělou inteligenci Lukáš Kačena.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Úplatky za ‚přivřené oči‘ nad podvodnými call centry. Na Ukrajině probíhá protikorupční operace Kartágo</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/ukrajina-kartago-korupce-nabu-sbu_2611130700_ula</link>
 <description>Ukrajinské protikorupční agentury NABU a SAP v září spustily operaci, kterou nazvaly Kartágo. Vyšetřovatelé se v ní zaměřují na činnost podvodných call center. Minulý týden přišli se zjištěním, že do jejich krytí před ukrajinskými úřady byli zapojení i nejvyšší představitelé bezpečnostních složek, včetně tajné služby nebo prokuratury. Za to, že nad činností falešných call center systematicky přivírali oči, dostávali úředníci od zločinců úplatky.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-112777298_261111-011520_ula.jpg?itok=htGTunxK" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 07:00:00 +0100</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Severokorejští hackeři ukradli podle FBI kryptoměny za více než 400 milionů dolarů. Pomoci jim měla AI</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/kldr-hackeri-severni-korea-kryptomeny-kradez-fbi-usa-ai_2611130658_raf</link>
 <description>Severokorejští hackeři podporovaní státem ukradli za posledních 18 měsíců kryptoměny v hodnotě více než 400 milionů dolarů (8,7 miliardy korun), přičemž zneužili tajně pořízené záznamy z webkamer. V noci na pátek to uvedl americký Federální úřad pro vyšetřování (FBI). Při podvodech hackeři údajně využívali i nástroje umělé inteligence, které jim pomáhaly vydávat se za jiné osoby při videohovorech. Severní Korea se k obvinění zatím nevyjádřila.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/bc4e6c81790f8d778d03e060149c34ef.jpg?itok=Mcfa8xUP" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 06:58:00 +0100</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>‚Bez nich to nemůžeme uzavřít.‘ Evropané budou podle Kushnera u mírových jednání</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-bez-nich-nemuzeme-uzavrit-evropane-budou-podle-kushnera-u-mirovych_2611130626_raf</link>
 <description>Evropští zástupci budou u vyjednávání o míru mezi Ruskem a Ukrajinou. Po čtvrtečním setkání v Dublinu to uvedli ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj a zvláštní americký vyslanec Jared Kushner, který spolu s kolegou Stevem Witkoffem do irské metropole dorazil z moskevského setkání s ruským prezidentem Vladimirem Putinem. Zelenskyj řekl, že další jednání budou následovat, píší agentury AFP a Reuters.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-11-12t214123z_2_261113-060850_raf.JPG?itok=sDjUxQuL" type="image/jpeg" />

A od začátku tahali za kratší konec a nakonec i prohráli 2:5.</description></item><item><title>Beats for Love Winter poprvé roztančí Brno. Dorazí Sara Landry i Sub Focus</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/905427-beats-for-love-winter-poprve-roztanci-brno-dorazi-sara-landry-i-sub-focus.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/905427-beats-for-love-winter-poprve-roztanci-brno-dorazi-sara-landry-i-sub-focus.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 18:03:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Kultura</category><description>Festival Beats for Love letos poprvé představí zimní edici. Brněnské výstaviště se 4. a 5. prosince promění v areál elektronické hudby se dvěma scénami, více než třiceti zahraničními umělci a bohatým doprovodným programem.</description></item><item><title>Průtah Libercem mezi ulicemi České mládeže a Hodkovickou se otevře už v sobotu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905718-prutah-libercem-mezi-ulicemi-ceske-mladeze-a-hodkovickou-se-otevre-uz-v-sobotu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905718-prutah-libercem-mezi-ulicemi-ceske-mladeze-a-hodkovickou-se-otevre-uz-v-sobotu.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:34:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>O týden dříve, než plánovalo, otevře Ředitelství silnic a dálnic silnici I/35 v Liberci v úseku mezi ulicemi České mládeže a Hodkovickou. Zprovozní ji v sobotu 14. listopadu odpoledne. Oprava za víc než 100 milionů trvala zhruba čtyři měsíce. Dvě krátké dokončovací etapy plánuje ŘSD na jaro 2027.</description></item><item><title>Trojzemí spojuje síly. Regiony chtějí společné investice a evropské dotace</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905443-trojzemi-spojuje-sily-regiony-chteji-spolecne-investice-a-evropske-dotace.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905443-trojzemi-spojuje-sily-regiony-chteji-spolecne-investice-a-evropske-dotace.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:43:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Liberecký kraj, německý zemský okres Görlitz a polský okres Zgorzelec podepsaly memorandum o vzniku přeshraničního seskupení. V Drážďanech na něj navázala dohoda se Saskem a Dolním Slezskem. Cílem je získat evropské dotace v letech 2028–2034 na dopravu, vzdělávání i transformaci po těžbě.</description></item><item><title>Rumunští podvodníci se objevili v Liberci. Vybírají na postižené</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905658-rumunsti-podvodnici-se-objevili-v-liberci-vybiraji-na-postizene.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905658-rumunsti-podvodnici-se-objevili-v-liberci-vybiraji-na-postizene.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 13:42:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>V Liberci se po nějaké době opět objevili rumunští podvodníci. Redakci na jejich přítomnost upozornil jeden ze čtenářů. Jejich postup je stále stejný, předstírají, že jsou hluchoněmí a vybírají peníze do sbírky na postižené.</description></item><item><title>Potravinová banka v Liberci se připravuje na sobotní sbírku, regály jsou prázdné</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905674-potravinova-banka-v-liberci-se-pripravuje-na-sobotni-sbirku-regaly-jsou.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905674-potravinova-banka-v-liberci-se-pripravuje-na-sobotni-sbirku-regaly-jsou.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 13:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Potravinová banka v Liberci se připravuje na sobotní sbírku, její regály zejí prázdnotou. Zbývá paleta těstovin, kdyby se denně nesvážely čerstvé potraviny jako pečivo, ovoce a zelenina či mléčné výrobky s končícím datem spotřeby ze supermarketů, neměla by už banka potřebným lidem co nabídnout.</description></item><item><title>Obchvat Svoru za půl miliardy se otevírá. Dlouhá uzavírka končí</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905678-obchvat-svoru-za-pul-miliardy-se-otevira-dlouha-uzavirka-konci.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905678-obchvat-svoru-za-pul-miliardy-se-otevira-dlouha-uzavirka-konci.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:01:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Po dvou letech otevírá Ředitelství silnic a dálnic (ŘSD) obchvat Svoru na silnici I/9. Stavba necelé dva kilometry dlouhého úseku přinesla dlouhou uzavírku a vyšla na více než půl miliardy korun.</description></item><item><title>Víkend přinese slunce. Poté se vrátí déšť</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905654-vikend-prinese-slunce-pote-se-vrati-dest.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905654-vikend-prinese-slunce-pote-se-vrati-dest.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Nadcházející víkend slibuje sice nižší teploty, ale návrat slunečného počasí. Začátkem příštího týdne se pak dokonce oteplí, ale s oteplením přijde návrat dešťových srážek.</description></item><item><title>Ztracená seniorka z Liberce je živá. Našli ji asistenti prevence kriminality</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905659-nevideli-jste-tuto-zenu-ztratila-se-v-liberci-patra-po-ni-policie-i-rodina.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905659-nevideli-jste-tuto-zenu-ztratila-se-v-liberci-patra-po-ni-policie-i-rodina.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:49:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Skvělá zpráva rezonuje Libercem. Třiasedmdesátiletá seniorka, která se ve čtvrtek ztratila a nedošla domů, byla v pátek nalezena živá a komunikovala. Nalezli ji asistenti prevence kriminality, kteří úzce spolupracují s Městskou policií Liberec. Žena je v péči lékařů.</description></item><item><title>Zubní pohotovosti v Liberci zůstávají. Jedna je v Dunaji, druhá v nemocnici</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905595-zubni-pohotovosti-v-liberci-zustavaji-jedna-je-v-dunaji-druha-v-nemocnici.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905595-zubni-pohotovosti-v-liberci-zustavaji-jedna-je-v-dunaji-druha-v-nemocnici.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 06:25:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Dobrá zpráva pro pacienty v Libereckém kraji. Obě zubní pohotovosti v Liberci, ta v paláci Dunaj i ta v areálu Krajské nemocnice Liberec, v příštím roce zůstávají. K dispozici jsou těm, kteří potřebují řešit akutní bolest zubů o víkendech a svátcích, každá v jinou dobu. Jedna na druhou navazuje.</description></item></channel></rss>

V listopadu 2026 pro vás kromě Slavnosti světel s lampionovým průvodem a tvořením nejen pro děti, která se koná již tuto sobotu 14. 11. 2026 od 15:30, chystáme také přednášku o živelních pohromách na střeše světa, jejich možných příčinách a spojitosti se změnou klimatu, se kterou za námi v neděli 15. listopadu 2026 přijede Jan Kropáček z Přírodovědecké fakulty UK.

Obě akce se konají v Tibetském domě na Asijské poznávací stezce ve Velkém Šenově.

Srdečně zve spolek Thonmi z.s.

Ve středu 11. listopadu 2026 se ve varnsdorfské tělocvičně uskutečnilo 4. kolo Podzimních her, tentokrát v košíkové. Do turnaje se zapojila družstva dívek a chlapců ze čtyř škol, která mezi sebou změřila síly a předvedla řadu napínavých sportovních soubojů.

Turnaj se hrál systémem každý s každým, přičemž jednotlivá utkání trvala 2 × 8 minut. Na palubovce nechybělo nasazení, bojovnost, týmová spolupráce ani touha po vítězství.

ZŠ Edisonova
ZŠ Náměstí
Gymnázium Varnsdorf
ZŠ Východní

Konečné pořadí – chlapci
Gymnázium Varnsdorf
ZŠ Náměstí
ZŠ Východní
ZŠ Edisonova

Dvě stříbrná umístění pro naši školu!

Naši žáci a žákyně ze ZŠ Náměstí předvedli krásné, bojovné a obětavé výkony. V každém utkání nechali na hřišti maximum, bojovali o každý míč a ukázali, že týmový duch a vzájemná podpora jsou základem úspěchu.

Velkou radost nám udělala obě naše družstva, která si v silné konkurenci vybojovala shodně krásné 2. místo! Všem našim hráčům a hráčkám patří velká pochvala a poděkování za parádní reprezentaci školy. Jsme na vás pyšní!

Děkujeme také všem zúčastněným školám za pěkné sportovní souboje a těšíme se na další kolo Podzimních her!

Mgr. Lukáš Hůla, ZŠ Varnsdorf, nám. E. Beneše, koordinátor turnaje
